}

\newsavebox{\ealboxen}

% a tier 3 word, in English and in translation alike
\newcommand{\ealkey}[1]{\textcolor{ealkeycolour}{#1}}
\newcommand{\ealkeytr}[1]{\textcolor{ealkeycolour}{\ealtext{#1}}}

% One translated word above one English word. Built from kernel
% primitives, never a tabular, which would break wherever the sheet
% loads array, booktabs or tabularx. The box is as wide as the wider of
% the two, so a long translation pushes its neighbours aside instead of
% overlapping them, and it claims its full height so a table row or a
% TikZ node makes room for it.
\newcommand{\ealgloss}[2]{%
  \sbox{\ealboxen}{\ealkey{#1}}%
  \sbox{\ealboxtr}{\small\textcolor{ealtwocolour}{\ealtext{#2}}}%
  \setlength{\ealglosswd}{\wd\ealboxen}%
  \ifdim\wd\ealboxtr>\ealglosswd\setlength{\ealglosswd}{\wd\ealboxtr}\fi
  \leavevmode
  \makebox[\ealglosswd][c]{%
    \makebox[0pt][c]{\usebox{\ealboxen}}%
    \makebox[0pt][c]{\raisebox{\ealglossraise}{\usebox{\ealboxtr}}}%
  }%
}

% opens up line spacing around a block of glosses, so the raised
% translations sit clear of the line above
\newenvironment{ealglossed}{\par\linespread{2.1}\selectfont\ignorespaces}{\par}

% a whole translated sentence above its English counterpart. block level,
% so it does not belong inside a tabular cell
\newcommand{\ealpara}[2]{%
  \par\addvspace{0.5\baselineskip}%
  {\color{ealtwocolour}\ealtextblock{#1}}%
  \penalty200
  {\color{ealenglish}#2\par}%
  \addvspace{0.5\baselineskip}%
}

\begin{frame}{Starter 1}

\vspace{-2.5em}

\begin{columns}[T]

\column{0.30\textwidth}
\begin{center}
\vspace{3em}
\ealpara{\ealkeytr{Oś liczbowa} A; \ealkeytr{Oś liczbowa} B}{\ealkey{Numberline} A; \ealkey{Numberline} B}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.95]

% --- Line A: 0 to 10, ticks every 1 ---
\node[font=\tiny\bfseries, anchor=west] at (-0.1,4.6) {\ealkey{Numberline} A};
\draw[thick] (-0.1,3.8) -- (3.1,3.8);
\foreach \x in {0,0.3,0.6,0.9,1.2,1.5,1.8,2.1,2.4,2.7,3}
  \draw (\x,3.7) -- (\x,3.9);
\foreach \x/\lab in {0/0,1.5/5,3/10} \node[font=\tiny] at (\x,3.5) {\lab};
% Given points: P at 3, Q at 8. Kept low, so they stay clear of the Line A heading.
\draw[blue, thick] (0.9,3.9) -- (0.9,4.1);
\node[blue, font=\tiny] at (0.9,4.28) {P};
\draw[blue, thick] (2.4,3.9) -- (2.4,4.1);
\node[blue, font=\tiny] at (2.4,4.28) {Q};
% --- Q3 answer: 6 marked on Line A ---
\draw[ans] (1.8,3.9) -- (1.8,4.1);
\node[anslab] at (1.8,4.28) {$6$};

% --- Numberline B: 0 to 1 in tenths ---
\node[font=\tiny\bfseries, anchor=west] at (-0.1,3.05) {\ealkey{Numberline} B};
\draw[thick] (-0.1,2.1) -- (3.1,2.1);
\foreach \x in {0,0.3,0.6,0.9,1.2,1.5,1.8,2.1,2.4,2.7,3}
  \draw (\x,2.0) -- (\x,2.2);
\foreach \x/\lab in {0/0,1.5/0.5,3/1} \node[font=\tiny] at (\x,1.8) {\lab};
% Given points: S at 0.3, T at 0.9
\draw[blue, thick] (0.9,2.2) -- (0.9,2.5);
\node[blue, font=\tiny] at (0.9,2.7) {S};
\draw[blue, thick] (2.7,2.2) -- (2.7,2.5);
\node[blue, font=\tiny] at (2.7,2.7) {T};
% --- Q3 answer: 0.45 marked on Line B, raised clear of the blue S label ---
\draw[ans] (1.35,2.2) -- (1.35,2.75);
\node[anslab] at (1.35,2.95) {$0.45$};

% --- Place value chart for 407.52 ---

\foreach \i/\head/\digit in {0/100/4,1/10/0,2/1/7,3/{$\cdot$}/{$\cdot$},4/0.1/5,5/0.01/2} {
  \draw ({0.5*\i},0.2) rectangle ({0.5*\i+0.5},0.7);
  \node[font=\tiny] at ({0.5*\i+0.25},0.95) {\head};
  \node[font=\small] at ({0.5*\i+0.25},0.45) {\digit};
}

\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

\column{0.70\textwidth}

\small
\begin{multicols}{2}
\begin{enumerate}\qtight

  \item \ealpara{Na \ealkeytr{osi liczbowej} A jakie liczby są zaznaczone przez $P$ i $Q$? \ashow{$3$ i $8$}}{On \ealkey{numberline} A what numbers are marked by $P$ and $Q$? \ashow{$3$ and $8$}}

  \item \ealpara{Na \ealkeytr{osi liczbowej} B jakie liczby są zaznaczone przez $S$ i $T$? \ashow{$0.3$ i $0.9$}}{On \ealkey{numberline} B what numbers are marked by $S$ and $T$? \ashow{$0.3$ and $0.9$}}

  \item \ealpara{Zaznacz $6$ na linii A i $0.45$ na linii B.}{Mark $6$ on Line~A and $0.45$ on Line~B.}

  \item \ealpara{Sam mówi, że $P=4$, ponieważ to jest $4$. zaznaczenie. Co zrobił źle? \ashow{Liczył zaznaczenia, a nie kroki: $P=3$}}{Sam says $P=4$, as it is the $4$th mark. What has he done wrong? \ashow{Counted marks, not steps: $P=3$}}

  \item \ealpara{Tabela pokazuje $407.52$. Ile jest warte $4$? A ile $5$? \ashow{$400$ i $0.5$}}{The chart shows $407.52$. What is the $4$ worth? And the $5$? \ashow{$400$ and $0.5$}}


  \item \ealpara{Oblicz $407.52\times 10$ i $407.52\div 10$. \ashow{$4075.2$ i $40.752$}}{Work out $407.52\times 10$ and $407.52\div 10$. \ashow{$4075.2$ and $40.752$}}

  \item \ealpara{\ealkeytr{Oś liczbowa} biegnie od $3.6$ do $3.7$ w $10$ równych krokach. Co jest $3$ kroki dalej od $3.6$? \ashow{$3.63$}}{A \ealkey{numberline} goes $3.6$ to $3.7$ in $10$ equal steps. What is $3$ steps along from $3.6$? \ashow{$3.63$}}

  \item \ealpara{Użyj $7$, $5$, $4$, $2$ i \ealkeytr{przecinka dziesiętnego}, aby utworzyć największą liczbę \ealkeytr{mniejszą niż} $100$. \ashow{$75.42$}}{Use $7$, $5$, $4$, $2$ and a \ealkey{decimal point} to make the largest number \ealkey{less than} $100$. \ashow{$75.42$}}

\end{enumerate}
\end{multicols}

\end{columns}

\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Starter 2: \ealkey{Inequality} Symbols \& Ordering \ealkey{Decimals}}

\begin{columns}[T]

\column{0.28\textwidth}
\vspace{5em}
\begin{center}
\ealpara{Linia A; \ealkeytr{Tabela wartości pozycyjnych}}{Line A; \ealkey{Place value} chart}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=1.1]

% --- Line A: 0.3 to 0.4 in hundredths ---
\node[font=\tiny\bfseries, anchor=west] at (-0.1,3.5) {Line A};
\draw[thick] (-0.1,2.6) -- (3.1,2.6);
\foreach \x in {0,0.3,0.6,0.9,1.2,1.5,1.8,2.1,2.4,2.7,3}
  \draw (\x,2.5) -- (\x,2.7);
\foreach \x/\lab in {0/0.3,1.5/0.35,3/0.4} \node[font=\tiny] at (\x,2.3) {\lab};
% --- Q5 answer: 0.38 marked ---
\draw[ans] (2.4,2.7) -- (2.4,3.0);
\node[anslab] at (2.4,3.2) {$0.38$};

% --- Place value chart: 0.4, 0.35, 0.405 ---
\node[font=\tiny\bfseries, anchor=west] at (-0.1,1.75) {\ealkey{Place value} chart};
\foreach \i/\head in {0/1,1/{$\cdot$},2/0.1,3/0.01,4/0.001}
  \node[font=\tiny] at ({0.6*\i+0.3},1.4) {\head};
\foreach \j in {0,1,2} {
  \foreach \i in {0,1,2,3,4}
    \draw ({0.6*\i},{-0.5*\j+1.15}) rectangle ({0.6*\i+0.6},{-0.5*\j+0.65});
}
% row 1: 0.4
\foreach \i/\d in {0/0,1/{$\cdot$},2/4} \node[font=\small] at ({0.6*\i+0.3},0.9) {\d};
% row 2: 0.35
\foreach \i/\d in {0/0,1/{$\cdot$},2/3,3/5} \node[font=\small] at ({0.6*\i+0.3},0.4) {\d};
% row 3: 0.405
\foreach \i/\d in {0/0,1/{$\cdot$},2/4,3/0,4/5} \node[font=\small] at ({0.6*\i+0.3},-0.1) {\d};

\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

\column{0.72\textwidth}

\small
\begin{multicols}{2}
\begin{enumerate}\qtight

  \item \ealpara{Wpisz $<$ lub $>$: $7 \mathrel{\text{\ashow{$<$}}} 12$ \newline $30 \mathrel{\text{\ashow{$>$}}} 3$}{Fill in $<$ or $>$: $7 \mathrel{\text{\ashow{$<$}}} 12$ \newline $30 \mathrel{\text{\ashow{$>$}}} 3$}
  \vspace{1em}

  \item \ealpara{W $0.405$, ile jest warte $4$? \ashow{$4$ \ealkeytr{części dziesiąte}, $0.4$}}{In $0.405$, what is the $4$ worth? \ashow{$4$ \ealkey{tenths}, $0.4$}}

  \item \ealpara{Na \ealkeytr{tabeli wartości pozycyjnych}, co jest większe, $0.4$ czy $0.35$? Dlaczego? \ashow{$0.4$: $4$ \ealkeytr{części dziesiąte} są \ealkeytr{większe niż} $3$ \ealkeytr{części dziesiąte}}}{On the \ealkey{place value} chart, which is bigger, $0.4$ or $0.35$? Why? \ashow{$0.4$: $4$ \ealkey{tenths} is \ealkey{greater than} $3$ \ealkey{tenths}}}

  \item \ealpara{Wpisz $<$, $>$ lub $=$ $0.4 \mathrel{\text{\ashow{$=$}}} 0.40$, $0.6 \mathrel{\text{\ashow{$>$}}} 0.06$}{Fill in $<$, $>$ or $=$ $0.4 \mathrel{\text{\ashow{$=$}}} 0.40$, $0.6 \mathrel{\text{\ashow{$>$}}} 0.06$}

\vspace{0.5em}

  \item \ealpara{Zaznacz $0.38$ na linii A. Czy jest bliżej $0.3$ czy $0.4$? \ashow{bliżej $0.4$}}{Mark $0.38$ on Line A. Is it nearer $0.3$ or $0.4$? \ashow{nearer $0.4$}}

  \columnbreak

  \item \ealpara{Uporządkuj od najmniejszej: $0.5$, $0.45$, $0.405$, $0.54$ \ashow{$0.405$, $0.45$, $0.5$, $0.54$}}{Order, smallest first: $0.5$, $0.45$, $0.405$, $0.54$ \ashow{$0.405$, $0.45$, $0.5$, $0.54$}}

  \vspace{0.2em}

  \item \ealpara{Prawda czy fałsz: więcej \ealkeytr{cyfr} \emph{po} \ealkeytr{przecinku dziesiętnym} oznacza większą liczbę? Podaj przykład/kontrprzykład. \ashow{Fałsz: $0.9>0.1234$}}{True or false: more \ealkey{digits} \emph{after} the \ealkey{decimal point} means a bigger number? Give an example/counter-example. \ashow{False: $0.9>0.1234$}}

  \vspace{0.2em}

  \item \ealpara{Alfie mówi, że $0.45>0.5$, ponieważ $45>5$. Wyjaśnij jego błąd, a następnie zapisz \ealkeytr{ułamek dziesiętny} między $0.4$ a $0.405$. \ashow{$0.5$ ma $5$ \ealkeytr{części dziesiąte}; np.\ $0.402$}}{Alfie says $0.45>0.5$ as $45>5$. Explain his mistake, then write a \ealkey{decimal} between $0.4$ and $0.405$. \ashow{$0.5$ has $5$ \ealkey{tenths}; e.g.\ $0.402$}}

\end{enumerate}
\end{multicols}

\end{columns}

\begin{columns}[T]

\begin{center}
\ealpara{Termometr ($^\circ$C); Linia C; $\leq$: \ealkeytr{mniejsze lub równe}}{Thermometer ($^\circ$C); Line C; $\leq$: \ealkey{less than or equal to}}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.85]

% --- Thermometer: -10 to 10, one tick every 2 degrees, only -10/0/10 labelled ---
\node[font=\tiny\bfseries, anchor=west] at (-0.1,3.45) {Thermometer ($^\circ$C)};
\draw[thick] (0.6,0) -- (0.6,3);
\foreach \y in {0,0.3,0.6,0.9,1.2,1.5,1.8,2.1,2.4,2.7,3}
  \draw (0.5,\y) -- (0.7,\y);
\foreach \y/\lab in {0/{$-10$},1.5/{$0$},3/{$10$}}
  \node[font=\tiny, anchor=east] at (0.4,\y) {\lab};
\fill[gray!40] (0.6,-0.3) circle (0.22);
\draw[gray!60, thick] (0.6,-0.3) circle (0.22);
% Given readings: A at -6, B at 4 (both sit exactly on a tick)
\draw[blue, thick] (0.7,0.6) -- (1.0,0.6);
\node[blue, font=\tiny, anchor=west] at (1.05,0.6) {A};
\draw[blue, thick] (0.7,2.1) -- (1.0,2.1);
\node[blue, font=\tiny, anchor=west] at (1.05,2.1) {B};

% --- Line C: -1 to 0 in tenths ---
\node[font=\tiny\bfseries, anchor=west] at (-0.1,-0.85) {Line C};
\draw[thick] (-0.1,-1.8) -- (3.1,-1.8);
\foreach \x in {0,0.3,0.6,0.9,1.2,1.5,1.8,2.1,2.4,2.7,3}
  \draw (\x,-1.9) -- (\x,-1.7);
\foreach \x/\lab in {0/{$-1$},1.5/{$-0.5$},3/{$0$}} \node[font=\tiny] at (\x,-2.1) {\lab};
% Reminder for the challenge question, which is the deck's only use of a weak inequality
\node[font=\tiny, anchor=west] at (-0.1,-2.7) {$\leq$: \ealkey{less than or equal to}};
% --- Q5 answers: -0.5 and -0.05 marked on Line C, at different heights ---
\draw[ans] (1.5,-1.7) -- (1.5,-1.4);
\node[anslab] at (1.5,-1.2) {$-0.5$};
\draw[ans] (2.85,-1.7) -- (2.85,-1.05);
\node[anslab] at (2.85,-0.85) {$-0.05$};

\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

\column{0.70\textwidth}

\small
\begin{multicols}{2}
\begin{enumerate}\qtight

  \item \ealpara{Co jest zimniejsze, $4\,^\circ$C czy $-4\,^\circ$C? \ashow{$-4\,^\circ$C}}{Which is colder, $4\,^\circ$C or $-4\,^\circ$C? \ashow{$-4\,^\circ$C}}

  \item \ealpara{Ile jest warte każde zaznaczenie na termometrze? Zapisz temperatury w A i B. \ashow{$2\,^\circ$C na zaznaczenie; A $=-6$, B $=4$}}{What is each mark on the thermometer worth? Write the temperatures at A and B. \ashow{$2\,^\circ$C per mark; A $=-6$, B $=4$}}

  \item \ealpara{Co jest zimniejsze, $-3$ czy $-8$? Wpisz: $-3 \mathrel{\text{\ashowq{$>$}}} -8$ \ashow{($-8$ jest zimniejsze)}}{Which is colder, $-3$ or $-8$? Fill in: $-3 \mathrel{\text{\ashowq{$>$}}} -8$ \ashow{($-8$ is colder)}}

  \item \ealpara{Uporządkuj od najmniejszej: $-2$, $5$, $-7$, $0$, $-1$ \ashow{($-7,-2,-1,0,5$)}}{Order, smallest first: $-2$, $5$, $-7$, $0$, $-1$ \ashow{($-7,-2,-1,0,5$)}}

  \columnbreak

  \item \ealpara{Zaznacz $-0.5$ i $-0.05$ na linii C. Co jest większe? \ashow{$-0.05$}}{Mark $-0.5$ and $-0.05$ on Line C. Which is larger? \ashow{$-0.05$}}

  \item \ealpara{Wpisz $<$ lub $>$: $-4.5 \mathrel{\text{\ashowq{$<$}}} -4.05$, $-0.3 \mathrel{\text{\ashowq{$<$}}} 0.03$}{Fill in $<$ or $>$: $-4.5 \mathrel{\text{\ashowq{$<$}}} -4.05$, $-0.3 \mathrel{\text{\ashowq{$<$}}} 0.03$}

  \item \ealpara{(Rozszerzenie) Uporządkuj od najmniejszej: $-0.08$, $0.7$, $-0.8$, $-0.75$ \ashow{($-0.8$, $-0.75$, $-0.08$, $0.7$)}}{(Extension) Order, smallest first: $-0.08$, $0.7$, $-0.8$, $-0.75$ \ashow{($-0.8$, $-0.75$, $-0.08$, $0.7$)}}

  \item \ealpara{(Wyzwanie) Wypisz \ealkeytr{liczby całkowite} $n$: $-3\leq n<2$. Zapisz liczbę między $-0.5$ a $-0.4$. \ashow{$-3,-2,-1,0,1$; np.\ $-0.45$}}{(Challenge) List the \ealkey{integers} $n$: $-3\leq n<2$. Write a number between $-0.5$ and $-0.4$. \ashow{$-3,-2,-1,0,1$; e.g.\ $-0.45$}}

\end{enumerate}
\end{multicols}

\begin{frame}{Starter 4: \ealkey{Rounding} \ealkey{Integers}}

\vspace{-2.5em}

\begin{columns}[T]

\column{0.30\textwidth}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.85]

% --- Line A: 40 to 50, ticks every 1 ---
\node[font=\tiny\bfseries, anchor=west] at (-0.1,3.5) {Line A};
\draw[thick] (-0.1,2.6) -- (3.1,2.6);
\foreach \x in {0,0.3,0.6,0.9,1.2,1.5,1.8,2.1,2.4,2.7,3}
  \draw (\x,2.5) -- (\x,2.7);
\foreach \x/\lab in {0/40,1.5/45,3/50} \node[font=\tiny] at (\x,2.3) {\lab};
% Given point: 47
\draw[blue, thick] (2.1,2.7) -- (2.1,3.0);
\node[blue, font=\tiny] at (2.1,3.2) {$47$};

% --- Line B: 3400 to 3500, ticks every 10 ---
\node[font=\tiny\bfseries, anchor=west] at (-0.1,1.4) {Line B};
\draw[thick] (-0.1,0.5) -- (3.1,0.5);
\foreach \x in {0,0.3,0.6,0.9,1.2,1.5,1.8,2.1,2.4,2.7,3}
  \draw (\x,0.4) -- (\x,0.6);
\foreach \x/\lab in {0/3400,1.5/3450,3/3500} \node[font=\tiny] at (\x,0.2) {\lab};

\small
\begin{multicols}{2}
\begin{enumerate}\qtight

  \item \ealpara{Wpisz $<$ lub $>$: $-6 \mathrel{\text{\ashowq{$<$}}} -2$}{Fill in $<$ or $>$: $-6 \mathrel{\text{\ashowq{$<$}}} -2$}

  \item \ealpara{Linia A: czy $47$ jest bliżej $40$ czy $50$? \ealkeytr{Zaokrąglij} to do \ealkeytr{najbliższych} $10$. \ashow{bliżej $50$, więc $50$}}{Line A: is $47$ nearer $40$ or $50$? \ealkey{Round} it to the \ealkey{nearest} $10$. \ashow{nearer $50$, so $50$}}

  \item \ealpara{\ealkeytr{Zaokrąglij} $32$ i $85$ do \ealkeytr{najbliższych} $10$: \ashow{$30$ i $90$}}{\ealkey{Round} $32$ and $85$ to the \ealkey{nearest} $10$: \ashow{$30$ and $90$}}

  \item \ealpara{Zaznacz $3472$ na linii B, a następnie \ealkeytr{zaokrąglij} to do \ealkeytr{najbliższych} $100$.}{Mark $3472$ on Line B, then \ealkey{round} it to the \ealkey{nearest} $100$.}

  \item \ealpara{\ealkeytr{Zaokrąglij} $3472$ do \ealkeytr{najbliższych} $10$; do \ealkeytr{najbliższych} $1000$. \ashow{$3470$ i $3000$}}{\ealkey{Round} $3472$ to the \ealkey{nearest} $10$; to the \ealkey{nearest} $1000$. \ashow{$3470$ and $3000$}}

  \item \ealpara{\ealkeytr{Zaokrąglij} $4950$ do \ealkeytr{najbliższych} $100$. \ashow{$5000$}}{\ealkey{Round} $4950$ to the \ealkey{nearest} $100$. \ashow{$5000$}}
  \columnbreak

  \item \ealpara{Zoe \ealkeytr{zaokrągla} $8449$ do \ealkeytr{najbliższych} $100$: $8449\to 8450\to 8500$. Jaki jest jej błąd? \ashow{Zaokrąglone dwa razy: tylko \ealkeytr{cyfra} dziesiątek $4$ się liczy, więc $8400$}}{Zoe \ealkey{rounds} $8449$ to the \ealkey{nearest} $100$: $8449\to 8450\to 8500$. What is her mistake? \ashow{Rounded twice: only the tens \ealkey{digit} $4$ counts, so $8400$}}

  \item \ealpara{\ealkeytr{Liczba całkowita} \ealkeytr{zaokrąglona} do \ealkeytr{najbliższych} $10$ to $250$. Jaka jest najmniejsza, jaką może być? A jaka największa? \ashow{$245$ i $254$}}{An \ealkey{integer} \ealkey{rounded} to the \ealkey{nearest} $10$ is $250$. What is the smallest it could be? What about the largest? \ashow{$245$ and $254$}}
  
  \item \ealpara{Czy możesz zapisać swoją poprzednią odpowiedź jako \ealkeytr{nierówność}? nazwij liczbę $n$ \ashow{$245\leq n\leq 254$}}{Can you write your previous answer as an \ealkey{inequality}? call the number $n$ \ashow{$245\leq n\leq 254$}}

\begin{frame}{Starter 5: \ealkey{Rounding} \ealkey{Decimals} \& \ealkey{Never-Ending Decimals}}

\vspace{-2.5em}

\begin{columns}[T]

\vspace{0.4em}
{\scriptsize
\ealpara{\ealkeytr{Nieskończone ułamki dziesiętne}}{\ealkey{Never-ending decimals}}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l@{}}
\textbf{\ealkey{Never-ending decimals}} \\[0.15em]
$\frac{2}{3} = 0.6666\ldots = 0.\dot{6}$ \\
$\frac{1}{7} = 0.142857142857\ldots$ \\
$\pi = 3.14159265\ldots$ \\
$\sqrt{2} = 1.41421356\ldots$ \\
$0.1010010001\ldots$
\end{tabular}}
\end{center}

\column{0.70\textwidth}

\small
\begin{multicols}{2}
\begin{enumerate}\qtight

  \item \ealpara{\ealkeytr{Zaokrąglij} $4738$ do \ealkeytr{najbliższych} $100$. \ashow{$4700$}}{\ealkey{Round} $4738$ to the \ealkey{nearest} $100$. \ashow{$4700$}}

  \item \ealpara{\ealkeytr{Zaokrąglij} do \ealkeytr{najbliższej} \ealkeytr{liczby całkowitej nieujemnej}: $4.6$, $12.348$ \ashow{($5$ i $12$)}}{\ealkey{Round} to the \ealkey{nearest} \ealkey{whole number}: $4.6$, $12.348$ \ashow{($5$ and $12$)}}

  \item \ealpara{Zaznacz $2.763$ na linii A. \ealkeytr{Zaokrąglij} to do $1$ \ealkeytr{miejsca dziesiętnego} (m.d.).}{Mark $2.763$ on Line A. \ealkey{Round} it to $1$ \ealkey{decimal place} (d.p.).}

  \item \ealpara{\ealkeytr{Zaokrąglij} do $1$ m.d.: $4.62$, $0.95$. Dlaczego $0.95$ to nie $1$? \ashow{$4.6$, $1.0$ --- $1$ m.d.\ wymaga jednej \ealkeytr{cyfry} \ealkeytr{ułamka dziesiętnego}}}{\ealkey{Round} to $1$ d.p.: $4.62$, $0.95$. Why is $0.95$ not $1$? \ashow{$4.6$, $1.0$ --- $1$ d.p.\ needs one \ealkey{decimal} \ealkey{digit}}}

  \item \ealpara{\ealkeytr{Zaokrąglij} $12.348$ do $2$ m.d., a następnie do $1$ m.d. Dlaczego nie $12.4$? \ashow{$12.35$, $12.3$ --- nigdy nie \ealkeytr{zaokrąglaj} dwa razy}}{\ealkey{Round} $12.348$ to $2$ d.p., then to $1$ d.p. Why not $12.4$? \ashow{$12.35$, $12.3$ --- never \ealkey{round} twice}}

  \columnbreak

  \item \ealpara{Linia B pokazuje $\frac{2}{3}=0.\dot{6}$. \ealkeytr{Zaokrąglij} to do $1$ m.d.\ i $2$ m.d. \ashow{$0.7$ i $0.67$}}{Line B shows $\frac{2}{3}=0.\dot{6}$. \ealkey{Round} it to $1$ d.p.\ and $2$ d.p. \ashow{$0.7$ and $0.67$}}

  \item \ealpara{(Rozszerzenie) Zapisz $\frac{1}{3}$ w \ealkeytr{notacji kropkowej}, a następnie \ealkeytr{zaokrąglij} $\frac{1}{7}$ do $3$ m.d. \ashow{$0.\dot{3}$ i $0.143$}}{(Extension) Write $\frac{1}{3}$ in \ealkey{dot notation}, then \ealkey{round} $\frac{1}{7}$ to $3$ d.p. \ashow{$0.\dot{3}$ and $0.143$}}

  \item \ealpara{(Wyzwanie) Które wymienione \ealkeytr{ułamki dziesiętne} nigdy nie tworzą \ealkeytr{okresu}? Czy któryś może być \ealkeytr{ułamkiem}? \ashow{$\pi$, $\sqrt{2}$, $0.101001\ldots$; tak: $0.\dot{3}=\frac13$}}{(Challenge) Which listed \ealkey{decimals} never settle into a \ealkey{repeating block}? Can one still be a \ealkey{fraction}? \ashow{$\pi$, $\sqrt{2}$, $0.101001\ldots$; yes: $0.\dot{3}=\frac13$}}

\end{enumerate}
\end{multicols}
